resources.string: On the box: SETUP › Phone shows the K1000 Wi-Fi code. Scan it once; the app keeps it and joins K1000 by itself from then on. Mobile data stays on for the rest of the phone. Phone already on K1000 (joined with the camera)? The app takes the Wi-Fi from the box by itself.
Or type the password printed under the code:
I joined K1000 in Android\'s Wi-Fi settings (fallback: the app then follows that K1000 network, and no other Wi-Fi)
Scan the Wi-Fi code on the K1000 screen
Without the camera the code cannot be scanned: type the password instead.

K1000 for Android %1$s
Free software: GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version. No warranty.
Source code: https://github.com/Maigre/K1000 (the app is in android/).

The notices and licences of everything in this app follow.
The phone is on the K1000 Wi-Fi: asking the box for it…
K1000 Wi-Fi taken from the box
The box\'s Wi-Fi is the one this app already joins.

The box\'s Wi-Fi is the one this app already has, but the app is not on it. If Android\'s dialog found no K1000 (“No devices found”): tick “I joined K1000 in Android\'s Wi-Fi settings” below, then Join K1000. Otherwise: Cancel, then Retry.
This box does not hand its Wi-Fi to the app (an older K1000, or no Wi-Fi password file on it): scan the code or type the password.
The Wi-Fi this phone is on does not answer with the K1000 certificate: nothing was taken from it.
The box\'s answer could not be used (%1$s): scan the code or type the password.
The box did not answer on this Wi-Fi: scan the code or type the password.
Without the nearby devices permission (local network), the app cannot ask the box for its Wi-Fi. Tap here to allow it.
The first time, Android asks to connect to “K1000”: tap Connect. Stay near the box.
Waiting for K1000. Join it in Android\'s Wi-Fi settings (Settings › Network & internet › Internet). The app follows the K1000 network only (a 10.42.0.x address), never another Wi-Fi.
The phone left the K1000 Wi-Fi. It rejoins by itself as soon as the box is in range again.
The phone left the K1000 Wi-Fi (it may be on another Wi-Fi now). Rejoin K1000 in Android\'s Wi-Fi settings.
Wi-Fi is off. Turn it on: the app rejoins K1000 by itself.
K1000 was not found, or the connection was declined. Is the box on, with its Wi-Fi on (SETUP › Phone)?
Android refused to look for K1000: %1$s
The phone is on the K1000 Wi-Fi, but the box\'s page did not answer (%1$s). Is K1000 running, with the phone page on?

The phone is on the K1000 Wi-Fi, but Android does not let this app use it: usually a VPN that apps may not bypass (or “Block connections without VPN”). Turn the VPN off while you use K1000; the app tries again by itself every few seconds.
The box\'s certificate was refused: %1$s. The app talks only to a box with a certificate from the K1000 CA.
Android needs your permission for K1000 to reach the box on its own Wi-Fi (Nearby devices › local network). Tap Retry to allow it.
Its built-in K1000 certificate cannot be used (%1$s). Install a correct build.
K1000 app %1$s · Back again now: hide K1000
Hold a button to switch (a tap only explains). This bar closes by itself; MUTE stays free below.
Hold the button to do it
Classic page (v1) on this phone. Back › Hold: new page (v2) to return.
New page (v2) on this phone. Back › Hold: classic page (v1) to go back.
This box has no new page (v2) yet: the classic page (v1) is shown.
(nothing played: Touch feedback off in Android settings?)
Haptics: tick (a run), click, confirm, reject, long_press, confirm2, reject3 played.

Edge test, %1$d s left (the bars stay shown for it: full screen hides Back from every swipe). Swipe in from the left or right edge INSIDE an amber band: Back must NOT fire. Above or below a band it fires (counted here; K1000 stays).\nBack fired: %2$d
Edge test: Back count %1$d (0 = every swipe inside a band was kept from Back).
